newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Airline staff strike continues.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Airline staff strike continues.

text.p: A three-day old strike by ground staff of Philippine Airlines continued on Friday amid conflicting claims from the management and the union over how the strike was affecting airline operations.

A spokesman for Philippine Airlines (PAL) said nine international flights and 24 domestic flights were cancelled on Friday as a result of the strike, which started on Wednesday over a new wage package.
But an official of PAL Employees Association (PALEA) said 49 flights were cancelled.
The number of flights meant to operate was not known because the airline had rearranged its schedule because of the strike, the PAL official said.
A PAL statement said the airline expected to begin normalizing operations on Friday because the Department of Labour had ordered striking employees to report back to work.
But PALEA national secretary Jose Penas III said the union had not officially received the department's letter.
"The strike is on. We are still going strong," he said.
Penas said about 3,000 of PALEA's 9,000 members were participating in the strike but the management said the strikers numbered less than 400.
It is the third strike to hit the financially-troubled national carrier in two years. PALEA struck twice in 1994, the first stoppage lasting a day and the second nine days.
